newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to scrap spacecraft after docking snag - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia to scrap spacecraft after docking snag - Tass.

text.p: Russian space engineers have given up their attempts to dock an unmanned cargo craft with the Mir space station and will let the vehicle drift off to burn up in the atmosphere, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Thursday.

The craft, a Progress M-33 in orbit since November 1996, had de-docked from Mir on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 craft which brought up a replacement crew. But efforts to link it back to the mother ship have failed since then.
According to Itar-Tass, which quoted Russian mission control, the Progress will be sent into a lower orbit and then will burn up in the upper layers of the Earth's atmosphere.
Mission control officials contacted late on Thursday could not confirm the report, but said top space officials would make a statement on the issue on Friday.
The report marks the latest in a series of setbacks for Russia's financially troubled space programme.
On February 23, a fire broke out on board the 11-year-old Mir, forcing the crew, which at the time included a German and an American as well as four Russian, to don gas masks.
At the moment, Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger are on Mir.
Last week, Russia's space agency announced it would again postpone the launch of the main living quarters it is scheduled to build for the Alpha international space station.
The delay, caused by cash trouble, has cast new doubts over Moscow's ability to participate in the multinational effort.
